name: useChannelSounding
summary: Bluetooth LE Channel Sounding availability and real ranging sessions against a Bluetooth peer.
plain: Reports whether this phone declares Bluetooth Channel Sounding, and measures the distance to a second Bluetooth device whose address you supply. Nothing is measured without a peer.
description: Support, adapter state and ranging service readiness come from the android.hardware.bluetooth_le.channel_sounding feature flag, a lookup of the ranging HAL service (IBluetoothChannelSounding) and the Bluetooth adapter, carrying source hardware. rangingAvailability and supportedSecurityLevels are what android.ranging.RangingManager reports for BLE Channel Sounding (BleCsRangingCapabilities); they are null when the platform did not deliver them. startRanging(config) opens a real android.ranging.RangingSession (Android 16, API 36+, RAW session with BleCsRangingParams) with the peer at config.peerAddress. The call resolves true only when the platform reports the session open; otherwise it resolves false and sessionError carries a status such as needs_peer_address, channel_sounding_unsupported, channel_sounding_disabled, ranging_api_unavailable, bluetooth_disabled, permission_denied (android.permission.RANGING must be declared and granted), session_active, invalid_parameters or open_failed. Every measurement is an android.ranging.RangingData sample: a distance in metres, a confidence ('low', 'medium', 'high'), an RSSI when the platform supplied one, and a timestamp, each null when omitted. RangingData does not say whether phase-based ranging or round-trip time produced a sample, so the hook reports no method, channel count or accuracy figure. Nothing is simulated: with no peer answering, measurements stays empty.

returns.name: isEnabled
returns.desc: Whether the feature is declared and the Bluetooth adapter is on.

returns.name: serviceFound
returns.desc: Whether the lookup of the ranging HAL service found a service.

returns.name: rangingAvailability
returns.desc: RangingManager availability for BLE Channel Sounding: 'enabled', 'not_supported', 'disabled_user', 'disabled_regulatory' or 'disabled_user_restrictions'. Null until read, below Android 16, or when the platform did not report it.

returns.name: supportedSecurityLevels
returns.desc: Channel Sounding security levels (1 and/or 4) from BleCsRangingCapabilities. Null when the platform did not report them.

returns.name: isRanging
returns.desc: Whether the platform holds an open ranging session. Follows the platform's session events, not the last call.

returns.name: measurements
returns.desc: Latest platform sample per peer: `deviceAddress`, `distanceMeters` (null when the platform omitted it), `confidence` ('low', 'medium' or 'high', else null), `rssi`, `sessionId` and `timestampMs`. Empty until the peer answers.

returns.name: sessionInfo
returns.desc: Result of the last start request: `status`, `error`, `sessionId`, `peerAddress`, `serviceName`, `serviceAvailable`, `channelSoundingFeature`, `timestampMs`.

returns.name: sessionError
returns.desc: Status code and reason when the last start or stop did not succeed, for example `needs_peer_address: peerAddress is required`.

returns.name: error
returns.desc: Latest failure message, or `null`. Failures are also logged and counted.

returns.name: source
returns.desc: Where the numbers came from. There is no 'simulated' value: a reading is real, derived from real readings, or unavailable.

returns.name: startRanging
returns.desc: Opens a Channel Sounding ranging session with the peer at config.peerAddress.

returns.name: stopRanging
returns.desc: Closes the running ranging session and returns what the platform did.

returns.name: refresh
returns.desc: Re-probes the feature flag, HAL service and adapter state.

actions.name: startRanging(config)
actions.desc: Opens a real BLE Channel Sounding ranging session with the peer at config.peerAddress.

inputs.name: config
inputs.desc: `{ peerAddress: string, role?: 'initiator' | 'responder' (default 'initiator'), securityLevel?: 1 | 4, sightType?: 'unknown' | 'line_of_sight' | 'non_line_of_sight', locationType?: 'unknown' | 'indoor' | 'outdoor', updateRate?: 'normal' | 'infrequent' | 'frequent' }`. peerAddress is required: six colon-separated hex bytes such as "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF". The optional fields are passed to BleCsRangingParams; omitted means the platform default.

actions.output: Resolves true when the platform reported the session open; false with the status and reason in sessionError when the peer address is missing or malformed, the device or OS cannot range, Bluetooth is off, a permission is missing, another session is running, or the platform refused to open. sessionInfo is updated either way.

actions.name: stopRanging()
actions.desc: Closes the running Channel Sounding ranging session.
actions.output: Returns `{ wasActive, closed, sessionId, error, timestampMs }`: wasActive is false when nothing was running, and error carries a failure from the platform's stop or close. Returns null when the native module is absent.

actions.name: refresh()
actions.desc: Re-probes the feature flag, HAL service and adapter state.
actions.output: Returns `{ isSupported, isEnabled, serviceFound, hasChannelSoundingFeature, error }`, or null when the native module is absent.

agentNote: Channel Sounding ranges a specific Bluetooth peer that itself supports Channel Sounding. Never invent a peer address: it comes from the device you are ranging with (a scan result, a bonded device). Without one startRanging resolves false with needs_peer_address. The ranging API is android.ranging (Android 16+) and requires android.permission.RANGING, which the app must declare in its manifest and request at runtime; without it the status is permission_denied. Report an empty measurements list as 'no peer answered', not as zero distance, and do not state a phase-based or round-trip method, a channel count or a centimetre accuracy: the platform reports none of them.
